children: Gold futures turned lower Monday, snapping a three-session winning streak, as the market returned its focus to U.S. yields and the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy.

The dollar continued higher against major currencies, extending gains after the Fed's ​rate hike lifted the greenback more than 1% last week; a stronger dollar ​makes bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.

"We are seeing some lingering concerns among the bulls about tighter U.S. monetary policy, which has pushed the U.S. dollar index to a ​more than two-month high... those bearish elements are working against the ​precious metals," American Gold Exchange analyst Jim Wyckoff said in a note.
Traders are pricing in an ‌88% ⁠chance of a U.S. rate hike in December, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

"It's a tough environment for gold in the short term, and the macro trends we're seeing in pricing from the typical markets that feed into and influence the gold price suggest investors and traders will shy away from the yellow metal until these dynamics become more favorable," Pepperstone's head of research Chris Weston said in a note.

Gold fell alongside crude oil prices on easing concerns over disruptions to Saudi pipeline flows despite attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels, but growing expectations of a global cycle of interest-rate hikes are weighing on gold, as higher rates make the precious metal less attractive, Soojin Kim from MUFG said.
